primitives.name: Habit Strength Acquisition
primitives.verbatim_quote: 130 PRINCIPLES OF BEHAVIOR has been reinforced with one gram of the food fifteen times and that the reinforcement is then suddenly shifted to six grams on the next fifteen reinforcements.
primitives.latex: H(t) = H_0 \cdot (1 - e^{-\lambda t}) + \Delta H \cdot u(t - T)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H(t)': 'Habit strength (dimensionless)', 'H_0': 'Initial habit strength (dimensionless)', '\\lambda': 'Learning rate constant (s^{-1})', 't': 'Trial number (dimensionless)', 'T': 'Shift trial (dimensionless)', '\\Delta H': 'Increment in habit strength (dimensionless)', 'u(t - T)': 'Heaviside step function'}
primitives.assumptions: Exponential learning model, instantaneous shift at trial T, no carryover effects from previous reinforcement magnitude.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when \Delta H becomes large enough to violate habit strength upper bound (H(t) > 1).

primitives.verbatim_quote: Neglecting the presumptive perseverating influence of secondary reinforcement in the situation, the outcome is easily calculated by methods analogous to the determination of the two main curves of Figure 29.
primitives.assumptions: Secondary reinforcement effects are negligible; only primary reinforcement magnitude influences habit formation rate.

primitives.name: Dotted Curve Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is shown by the dotted curve rising from the one-gram curve at the fifteenth reinFig.
primitives.assumptions: Behavior continues along original trajectory until shift point, then immediately follows new trajectory based on updated parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Projection fails if there is a lag time before the new trajectory is adopted, introducing hysteresis.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Conformal prediction intervals for future outcomes assuming piecewise-stationary environments. GSE: State machines transition to new subroutines upon detecting regime changes indicated by projected thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Time difference between reinforcement shift and actual change in behavior pattern.

primitives.name: Reinforcement Magnitude Variation
primitives.verbatim_quote: In concluding our discussion of Figure 29 it is to be noted that exactly analogous curves would also be produced by suitable variations in the quality of the reinforcing agent.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q(H)': 'Quality-adjusted habit strength (dimensionless)', 'R_m': 'Reinforcement magnitude (e.g., grams of food)', 'R_q': 'Reinforcement quality factor (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Habit strength depends multiplicatively on both quantity and quality of reinforcement, with quality acting as an amplification parameter.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Quality factor approaches zero, rendering reinforcement ineffective regardless of magnitude.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models how different types of bets (high vs. low stakes) produce equivalent learning dynamics when adjusted for risk-reward tradeoff. GSE: Reinforcement signals from environment can be scaled by intrinsic motivation factors to predict skill acquisition.
layer2.telemetry: Comparative analysis of learning rates across different quality-reinforcement combinations.
